title: Noise rules, trust ladder and shadow report
bridge: The noise rules are like PR etiquette for one teammate: one open PR, drafts first, stale PRs closed. Except: the teammate is a routine, and the rules run as code before it opens anything. It even pauses itself when people keep closing its PRs.
intro: Our last dependency bot had 13 of its 14 PRs closed unreviewed. This lesson makes sure routines start quiet and earn attention. Noise rules ship before any routine. A trust ladder moves a routine up only on evidence. A weekly shadow report shows each owner what the routine would have done.

picture.caption: A routine earns its way from shadow to normal, and falls back a step the moment it misbehaves.

nodes.label: noise rules: one open PR, drafts, 7-day close

steps.text: may open a PR only if none of its PRs is open; always as a draft
one message per team a day: ready PRs, drafts, idle closes, pauses, cost
every Sunday: the routine's shadow fix next to what a person did
qualifies? a DM; the owner opens the PR that raises stage:
a false heal, a revert or under half merged: an override now, a PR to lower stage:
under half of the last 20 PRs merged: paused until the owner resumes it

p: The weekly dependency workflow in fcp opened PRs nobody had time for: 13 of its last 14 were closed unreviewed. A bot that people ignore teaches them to ignore bots. Routines must not repeat that.

So four noise rules ship before any routine. At most one open PR per routine. Every PR has a routine:<name> label and opens as a draft. A routine PR with no activity for 7 days is closed with a note. A daily digest replaces many pings, and a routine whose PRs keep getting closed pauses itself.
Renovate's own PRs are out of scope here. Renovate manages them on its monthly schedule (lesson g5-6).

callout.text: People's attention is the scarcest resource in the loop. A routine has to earn it with merged PRs, not spend it with noisy ones.

sections.h: One open PR, drafts, and the 7-day close
p: noise.ts holds two activities. mayOpenPr is part of routineRun's gate. If the routine already has an open PR, the run waits and re-checks hourly on a timer. It never opens a second PR.
closeIdlePrs runs daily at 03:23 from a schedule (lesson g5-2). Idle means no commit, comment or review for 7 days. It says why, closes the PR, and comments on the linked Jira ticket.

All GitHub calls go through the broker. Ask the broker owner (G3) for an orchestrator scope: read PRs, and comment on and close PRs labelled routine:*. The activity holds no token. Marking a PR ready is G4's ready gate, never this code.
sections.because: One open PR per routine means people only ever see one thing at a time from it.

sections.h: The merge rate and the auto-pause
p: mergeRate looks at the last 20 closed PRs labelled routine:<name> and returns the share that merged. With fewer than 20 there is no verdict, so a new routine is never paused on a handful of PRs.

Below 0.5, autoPause sets routine:<name>:paused in G3's flag store with the reason, and DMs the owner. preRunGate reads that flag before every run. Only the owner (or Sean) resumes it, with a Slack button.
The trust ladder reuses mergeRate for its demotion rule. Keep one function.
sections.because: A routine whose PRs people keep closing is noise, so it stops itself until its owner looks.

p: One short message a day replaces many pings. Each team (FE, BE, DevOps) gets one, in its channel from config/people.yaml. It runs at 06:37 Israel time, Sunday to Thursday.

It lists ready PRs waiting for review, drafts per owner, idle closes and paused routines with the reason. It also shows yesterday's cost per routine from the gateway's spend tags. On a day with no routine activity, it sends nothing.
sections.because: A quiet day that sends nothing keeps the digest worth reading on the days that matter.

sections.h: The trust ladder, part 1: down fast, up on evidence
p: Every routine has a stage. In shadow it runs on real triggers and opens nothing. In drafts it opens real draft PRs and pings only the owner. The owner may mark a good one ready, which sends it to the reviewer of the day. In normal, clean PRs are marked ready and the reviewer of the day is requested.
Demotion is one step down. It happens on a false heal, a revert within 14 days, or under half of the last 20 PRs merged. A false heal is a fix that makes CI green by weakening a test (lesson g5-5).
Promotion needs all three: the bench slice 50% solved, zero false heals, and 10 runs at this stage. Bug fixers must also reproduce at least 60%.
sections.because: Trust is earned from evidence and lost on the first sign of misbehaviour, so promotion is slow and demotion is immediate.

sections.h: The trust ladder, part 2: an override now, a PR for the file
p: evaluate runs daily for every routine at 05:51. A demotion takes effect at once through a flag, routine:<name>:stage_override. Then it opens a PR that lowers stage: in the charter, so the file stays the truth.
Promotion only goes through a PR that raises stage:. The daily job only DMs the owner that the routine qualifies. The owner opens or asks for that PR, and someone else approves it.
The effective stage is the lower of the charter's stage and the override. routineRun reads it at the start and stores it in the Stage search attribute.
sections.because: The flag acts in seconds when something goes wrong, and the PR keeps the charter the reviewed record of the stage.

p: Shadow mode helps only if someone looks at it. Every Sunday at 07:13, the report compares each shadow fix with what a person did for the same problem.

The human fix is one of three things. For red main, the commits up to the next green run. For a bug, its linked merged PR; for an upgrade, what the Renovate PR became. If the human added tests, they run on the routine's saved diff in a lite VM. That is the objective answer to "would it have worked".

A Sonnet 5.5 judge at medium effort answers three questions: same root cause, smaller or bigger, would a reviewer reject it. Check the judge on 10 labelled pairs first. One row per run goes to the weekly run review thread, not to team channels.
sections.because: The report shows each owner whether the routine would have helped, before it opens anything.

lab.title: Run the ladder in your head (reading lab)

worked.do: fe-ci-fixer has PR #2601 open. A new red main run reaches mayOpenPr. What happens?
worked.see: Gate.wait("fe-ci-fixer already has #2601 open"). The run parks and re-checks hourly. No VM, no second PR.

worked.do: A routine has 12 closed PRs, 3 merged. What does mergeRate return, and is it paused?
worked.see: undefined: fewer than 20 closed PRs. No verdict, so no pause.

worked.do: Now 20 closed, 8 merged. What does autoPause do?
worked.see: rate 0.4 < 0.5: it sets routine:<name>:paused with "only 40% of its last 20 PRs were merged" and DMs the owner.

worked.do: A routine in normal had one of its PRs reverted 9 days after merge. What does evaluate do?
worked.see: demotionReason returns "#<n> was reverted within 14 days". The override drops it to drafts now, a charter PR lowers stage:, and the owner gets a DM.

worked.do: A bug fixer in shadow: slice solved 55%, reproduced 50%, no false heals, 14 runs. Does it qualify for drafts?
worked.see: No. missingForPromotion returns ["reproduced 50% of bugs, needs 60%"].

worked.do: In the shadow report, the human fix added two tests. What is the objective answer, and where does it come from?
worked.see: Whether those tests pass on the routine's saved diff, run in a lite VM. The judge's verdict comes next to it.

lab.faded: Write the FE channel's digest for this day. Two ready PRs wait (one for 2 days), one draft is with the owner, one PR closed as idle. fe-dead-code is paused, and fe-ci-fixer cost $4.10 yesterday. The layout is given (one line per item); the order of the lines is left to you, most urgent first.
lab.alone: Write a RoutineStats object for a routine in drafts that qualifies for normal, and one that is demoted for a false heal. For each, say what evaluate does and which messages the owner gets.
lab.done: Given a routine's numbers, you can say its next stage and why, and what the owner hears.

quiz.q: A routine already has one open PR. A new trigger arrives for a different root cause. What does mayOpenPr do?

options.text: Opens a second PR, because the root cause is different
options.why: The rule is one open PR per routine, whatever the cause.

options.text: Returns wait; the run re-checks hourly and opens nothing until the first PR closes
options.why: People see one thing at a time from each routine.

options.text: Closes the old PR and opens the new one
options.why: Only the 7-day idle rule closes routine PRs.

quiz.q: How does a routine move from drafts to normal?

options.text: The daily job promotes it when the numbers qualify
options.why: The job only DMs the owner. Promotion is never automatic.

options.text: The owner opens a PR that raises stage: in the charter, and someone else approves it
options.why: Promotions only by reviewed PR; the owner never approves their own routine's PRs.

options.text: The reviewer of the day flips a flag in Slack
options.why: The flag store holds overrides for demotion, not promotion.

quiz.q: A false heal is found in a routine in normal. What happens, and how fast?

options.text: The override flag drops it one step now, and a PR lowers stage: in the charter
options.why: The flag acts at once; the PR keeps the file the truth.
It moves down one step. Pausing is the circuit breaker's job (lesson g5-4).
